item.title: Kuldeep or Saransh? The subplot thickens as Colombo braces for a different script
item.description: Kuldeep Yadav's absence from India's final training sessions has intensified the selection intrigue ahead of the Colombo Test, with Saransh Jain's strong showing in the nets and Sri Lanka's left-hand-heavy batting line-up adding weight to the off-spinner's case. The second Test between India and Sri Lanka will start from Sunday at the Sinhalese Sports Club ground in Colombo.

item.description: The finance commissioner of New York City missed a crucial city council hearing regarding the pied-à-terre tax due to ongoing litigation, opting instead to provide written statements. The release of property valuations raised concerns about privacy and clarity among residents. In response, council members are actively pursuing answers and have prepared a list of inquiries for the administration.

item.title: Meta sued by former manager who claims he was fired over immigration letter
item.description: A former Meta manager filed a lawsuit alleging wrongful termination after objecting to an immigration letter. James Tillinghast claimed the letter overstated an employee's contributions and responsibilities. He also alleged Meta provided preferential immigration support to certain Chinese national employees. Tillinghast believes his dismissal was retaliation for raising these concerns. The lawsuit names Meta Platforms and a manager as defendants.

item.title: Japan eradicated 10,000 mongooses in 2024, 30 were released in 1979 to kill snakes
item.description: In a remarkable environmental achievement, Japan has announced the successful elimination of invasive small Indian mongooses, resolving a long-standing ecological dilemma on its UNESCO World Heritage site. The culmination of rigorous trapping, tracking, and monitoring efforts has set the stage for a revitalization of local wildlife populations, positioning this program among the largest mongoose eradications observed globally.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: US seized California island ranch after $4m offer; jury awarded family $12.7m
item.description: A federal jury awarded a California family $12.7 million for their Santa Cruz Island ranch. The government had seized the 6,300-acre property using eminent domain in 1996. This verdict concluded a decades-long property dispute between park officials and the Gherini family. The family's ancestors had owned part of the island since the late 19th century. The award allowed the National Park Service to gain full control of the land.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: Medical debt relief model: MacKenzie Scott’s gifts erase $40 billion; $10 cancels $1,000
item.description: MacKenzie Scott pioneered large-scale medical debt relief through significant donations. Her gifts enabled the abolition of over forty billion dollars in medical debt. This initiative has provided relief to millions of families across all fifty states. Scott's model has also inspired other billionaires to contribute to debt eradication efforts. While philanthropic efforts offer immediate relief, systemic reforms are needed for lasting change.

item.title: Twist in double-murder suicide: Wife’s Rs 1.5 crore demand may have led to killings
item.description: A banker allegedly murdered his wife and sister in a double murder-suicide incident. Divya Mishra sought a Rs 1.5 crore financial settlement in her divorce proceedings. Strained relations over Manas Bajpayi's sister, Sheeba, also contributed to the marital discord. Police are investigating the killings as a pre-planned sequence of events. Digital evidence and witness statements are being analyzed to establish the motive.

item.title: Who is Sara Bejlek? 20-year-old stuns Sabalenka in Cincinnati Open run
item.description: Sara Bejlek reached her first WTA 1000 semifinal at the Cincinnati Open 2026. She defeated top players including world number one Aryna Sabalenka. Bejlek's impressive performance propelled her to a new career-high ranking. This success follows her earlier WTA singles title win in Abu Dhabi. The young Czech player is now a notable name in women's tennis.

item.title: Hockey World Cup: India's semifinal hopes end after 1-3 loss to Netherlands
item.description: The defeat leaves India without a point in the second round. India had already lost to England in the first round, and even a victory against Argentina on Monday would take them to only three points. That will not be enough to reach the semifinals. India will instead play in the fifth-eighth place classification matches after their final second-round game against Argentina.

item.title: FSSAI issued 150 notices to major food brands in recent months over misleading ads
item.description: India's food regulator FSSAI has issued over 150 notices to major food companies recently. These notices address misleading advertisements and non-compliance with labeling regulations. Action has been taken against brands like Nestle India and Coca-Cola India. E-commerce platforms Amazon and Flipkart also received multiple notices and a warehouse license cancellation. Food service establishments including KFC and McDonald's faced similar enforcement actions.
item.dc:creator: ANJALI SINGH

item.title: Being queer in Kashmir: Families, phones, friendships monitored, says report
item.description: A comprehensive report reveals the extensive control exerted over LGBTQIA+ individuals in Kashmir, highlighting issues such as monitored communications and scrutinized social interactions. The study emphasizes how family pressures and societal expectations surrounding marriage exacerbate marginalization. Additionally, educational institutions contribute to feelings of harassment and social exclusion. While some visibility fosters a degree of acceptance, it simultaneously increases the risk of backlash and surveillance for queer communities in the region.
item.dc:creator: NASEER GANAI

item.title: Dhols, chants and belief: How Delhi turned a World Championships semi-final into a homecoming
item.description: A packed Indira Gandhi Indoor Stadium created an unforgettable atmosphere as Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand battled China's top seeds in the BWF World Championships semi-finals. Chants, dhols and unwavering support drove the Indian pair throughout their 64-minute contest. Though the eventual bronze medallists fell short, Delhi's passionate crowd emerged as one of the tournament's defining stories.
item.dc:creator: TANUJ LAKHINA

item.title: 'Women are liable to no one': Rahul attacks 'Manusmriti' at Pune event
item.description: During a dynamic gathering in Pune, Rahul Gandhi championed women's independence and personal identity. However, discord erupted between student groups, necessitating police intervention and resulting in multiple arrests. Political factions exchanged blame over allegations of disrupted activities and financial support. The primary focus of the event was to confront significant student challenges, such as job scarcity and examination irregularities, against the backdrop of rising political tension related to youth agendas.
item.dc:creator: VIJAYA SRIVASTAVA

item.title: K'taka assembly passes apartment Bill: From ownership to redevelopment, rules defined
item.description: The Karnataka Assembly has passed a landmark bill to regulate apartment ownership and management effectively. This legislation lays the groundwork for Residents' Welfare Associations and offers guidance on managing common spaces. It also introduces a multi-tiered dispute resolution system. For redevelopment initiatives, a majority of 75% owner consent is now required, with owners who decline receiving double their property's assessed value.

item.title: Pullela Gopichand explains Treesa-Gayatri 's Worlds breakthrough
item.description: Chief badminton national coach Pullela Gopichand credited six weeks of tactical preparation, improved rotation and patience for Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand's historic bronze medal at the BWF World Championships in New Delhi. Despite their semi-final loss to China's Liu Sheng Shu and Tan Ning, Gopichand praised the duo's progress and expressed optimism for India's Asian Games campaign.

item.title: FIR against Dipke: CJP founder booked for 'entering school without permission'
item.description: Police registered a case against Abhijeet Dipke and others for entering a government school. They allegedly disrupted classes and threatened teachers during a campaign visit. The complaint stated Dipke recorded and shared the school visit on social media. He also made claims about students being brought to the school. Further investigation into the incident is currently underway by officials.

item.title: ‘Crushed his lungs’: How a ‘minor’ dispute ended in Adobe techie's death
item.description: A software engineer was allegedly beaten to death by his wife's relatives following a dispute. His family claims the attack was a pre-planned, calculated conspiracy to kill him. The assault occurred at his home in Delhi after his wife summoned her family members. Police have detained four individuals in connection with the brutal incident and are investigating. The case is being registered under sections relating to murder and common intention.

item.title: IIT Delhi student dies after jumping from sixth-floor campus building
item.description: A 31-year-old M.Sc. Physics student at IIT Delhi died Saturday morning. Police received a call about a student jumping from a building on campus. The injured student was taken to the hospital and declared brought dead. Investigators found no apparent injuries other than those from the fall. Police are examining the student's mobile phone and counselling records.
item.dc:creator: TNN

item.title: 'Sometimes dynastic politics has its benefits': Akhilesh on how 5 family MPs helped SP
item.description: Akhilesh Yadav pointed to the presence of multiple members of his family in the SP and suggested that this had helped prevent a split in the party. "Have you ever wondered why the entire party did not split? Because there are five MPs from the same family. We also have several Muslim MPs, and some staunch socialists, so our numbers would not decrease," he said.
item.dc:creator: RAJEEV SINGH

item.title: MP: One newborn dies, 2 suffer burn injuries after warmer machine catches fire
item.description: A newborn died and two others were injured after a warmer machine caught fire in Chhindwara's NICU. The incident occurred early Saturday morning due to sparks from the machine's filament. Hospital staff quickly extinguished the blaze using firefighting equipment. The injured babies were transferred to Jabalpur for advanced medical care. An inquiry has been initiated to determine the exact cause of the fire.
item.dc:creator: PRACHI KUMAWAT

item.title: After Root, Stokes calls ECB decision 'shambolic' over Headingley’s exclusion
item.description: Ben Stokes has taken a bold stance against the England and Wales Cricket Board after they decided to exclude Headingley and Old Trafford from the 2027 men's Ashes lineup. This controversial move has sparked backlash among players and fans due to the historical importance these venues hold within Ashes cricket.
item.dc:creator: TOI SPORTS DESK

item.title: 7-storey under construction building collapses in Hyderabad, 2 dead
item.description: In Madhapur, a seven-storey building that was still under construction collapsed tragically on Saturday afternoon. Search and rescue teams are actively working to locate any individuals who may be trapped beneath the rubble. Officials have sadly confirmed the death of at least two individuals due to the collapse. The building was reportedly erected on a cramped lot, and construction had previously ceased.
item.dc:creator: MAHESH BUDDI

item.title: Mumbai hit-and-run: US national, 15, knocked down by speeding biker
item.description: A 15-year-old American student was injured in a Juhu hit-and-run incident. A speeding motorcyclist struck the teen while she crossed the road near Bhaidas Hall. She sustained a concussion, leg bruises, and a jaw injury from the collision. Police have registered a case and are actively searching for the fleeing motorcyclist. Activists noted the absence of speedbreakers due to Metro construction work.
item.dc:creator: TNN

item.title: Congress’s renewed youth outreach: How CJP has forced parties to course correct
item.description: Student protests at Jantar Mantar have prompted political parties to rethink their youth engagement strategies. The Congress party is now focusing on youth issues and expanding its outreach programs nationwide. Rahul Gandhi's recent actions highlight the party's renewed commitment to addressing student concerns. The Congress Working Committee has proposed an education-to-employment roadmap for young people. This shift reflects a broader effort to regain support among the nation's youth.
item.dc:creator: KUNAL VARMA

item.title: 'Don't be desperate for wickets': Gautam Gambhir's message to Kuldeep Yadav
item.description: India returned to winning ways in the World Test Championship after a 165-run victory over Sri Lanka in the first Test at the Galle International Stadium on Wednesday. Four days after that win, the visitors will be back in action in Colombo for the second and final Test. India will be pleased with most aspects of their performance in Galle, but Kuldeep's form remains one of the major talking points.
item.dc:creator: TOI SPORTS DESK
